title: The ACS Redesign
body_text: Edit: the RSS feeds are back! I don't know why this couldn't have been done when the new web page designs rolled out, but you can find the feed addresses here. I'm also not sure why no one there got around to telling me (and many others) about this, but I am glad to have the functionality back. A longtime Pipeline reader just alerted me to this. But I'm not sure it's all back! At least in my reader (NewsBlur), the graphical abstracts are not displaying, which is not the idea, guys. I'd be glad to hear from other people using other software: are these feeds working for you? Can you see the entire abstracts? Because if not, that just barely counts as working. . . Below is the post as I wrote it this morning, for reference: Just time for a quick note today, and it’s going to be a complaint. I have not covered any interesting papers recently from any of the ACS journals, but I’m sure that it’s not because they haven’t published anything worth reading. It’s because I (and many others) use RSS feeds to browse these journals, and the recent redesign there broke every single feed. I wrote to complain about this, and got a rather generic response about how they are aware of this issue and how it has been brought to the attention of the appropriate technical team. At this time, they inform me, they are unable to provide an estimate of when this issue might be resolved. And so on. I can’t help but think that a journal web site had to have been completely aware of what an RSS feed is and how it’s used, and that breaking it was not some casual oversight. They appear to have had a reason to do this, so the “Oh, is something not working? Let’s get someone looking at that for you” type of reply is not exactly believable. Presumably they want All The Traffic to come directly through their sites, with none of this browsing abstracts from afar. But this is idiotically short-sighted. I am not going to make separate trips to all the ACS journals I used to follow by RSS in order to across through them manually (and what’s more, their ASAP pages have been altered to make them less usable as well). Not when I used to have everything in one place. “Enshittification” is the word for this sort of thing. And if the ACS was not trying to enshittify their journal-reading experience, I wish someone would send me something other than a form letter explaining what the idea was behind destroying the RSS functions. Can’t wait to hear it. You'll notice that I'm not even complaining about the loss of the old ACS logo and its replacement by something that looks like a sign for an airport hotel. I already suggested on Bluesky that if they'd get the RSS feeds working again that they could go all the way to having Chthulhu holding an Erlenmeyer flask and I'd be fine with it, and I see that now you can buy a mug with that design. Not official ACS merchandise, I hastily add. Fine by me!
